Where an artificial drain has been constructed within the boundary of one owner for the purpose of discharging surface water, the landowner is not under any obligation to keep the drain open for the purpose of draining the lands of others unless it is a substitute for a natural drain. 13
The Division can acquire drainage rights in an artificial ditch of another only by deed, prescription, or condemnation.
DEVELOPMENT OF AN EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM
fter the landowners have been informed of the proposed highway construction, an educational program must be initiate to provide information needed to develop drainage plans. The Extension Adviser shall provide the leadership in the educational program, with assistance from:
. the extension council
. the soil and water conservation district
the work-unit conservationist
d. the district highway engineer
e. the specialists from the Cooperative Extension Service of the College of Agriculture
The scope of the educational program will consider such items as:
a. A review of the Division's rights and responsibilities in the process of developing a highway program.
b. A review of the landowner's rights and responsibilities in areas where highway programs are developed.
c. Illustrations of the types of assistance available to the Division and landowners from other governmental agencies and private interests.
d. Identification of typical problems that may be encountered, and a review of possible solutions.
e. Ways in which the Division and landowners may exchange information and coordinate activities.
f. Gathering of pertinent information required by landowners to plan for drainage improvements.
